title: Meitei IDPs to Rally in Imphal on November 22, Seek Public Support for Return Home
summary: The Apex Committee of Meitei IDPs has appealed for public support for its November 22 rally in Imphal, demanding safe return and rehabilitation of displaced families.
body:
Imphal, November 19, 2026: The Apex Committee of Meitei Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), Manipur, has appealed to the public to extend moral support to a rally scheduled for November 22, demanding the safe return of displaced families to their original homes.

The proposed rally will be held under the theme “Eikhoi Keidoungei Eyumda Hanjil Hangani?”, which asks, “When will we be able to return to our homes?” The appeal was made by Naba Ningthoujam, Convenor of the Churachandpur Meitei United Committee, while speaking to media persons at the Manipur Press Club on Wednesday.

Ningthoujam said that the crisis which began on May 3, 2023, had forced thousands of Meitei people to leave their homes and take shelter in relief camps and other temporary locations. He highlighted the prolonged uncertainty faced by displaced families, many of whom continue to wait for conditions that would allow them to return to their respective localities.

According to the committee, the rally will begin at Keishampat and proceed towards Thangmeiband Thau Ground in Imphal. The organisers have urged people across the valley areas to participate and extend solidarity with families who continue to face the consequences of displacement.

Expressing concern over the continuing humanitarian situation, Ningthoujam said that many displaced families had lost their homes and sources of livelihood, while some had also lost family members during the prolonged crisis. He expressed disappointment over what he described as the absence of concrete initiatives by the Central and State governments to resolve the situation and establish a definite timeline for the safe return of IDPs.

The committee said the demonstration was intended to draw public attention to the continued hardships of displaced people and their demand for an early return to their original homes. It also called for meaningful dialogue and practical measures to address the concerns of affected families.

The demand for the return and rehabilitation of internally displaced persons remains one of the major challenges arising from the violence that erupted in Manipur in May 2023. For families who have spent years away from their homes, the question of security, rehabilitation and the restoration of normal life continues to be a pressing concern.

The November 22 rally is expected to provide a common platform for displaced families and supporters to express their grievances and urge the authorities to take concrete steps towards a safe and dignified return.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
